- When sentiment is 0.00 across recent days, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon and undercorrect later — apply a downward bias correction for the first 5–7 days of forecast.
- If the last 18-day history includes a spike (e.g., +1.00+ above mean), model often overshoots and fails to revert — apply a mean-reversion penalty to subsequent days, especially if sentiment remains flat.
- When sentiment is 0.00 and model forecast is >85.00, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 units for next 3–5 days to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If model forecast is consistently 0.5–1.0 above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “lag correction” — subtract 0.2–0.5 from forecast for next 2–3 days.
- For sentiment history with no positive sentiment, model tends to underestimate the “bottom” of the range — adjust downward by 0.3–0.7 for the first 3–5 days of forecast.
- If model forecast is >86.00 and true outcome is <84.00, apply a “spike decay” rule — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 per day for 3–5 days after spike.
